rounds.text: Despite headline profit growth, Shayona Engineering Ltd suffers from a severe cash flow disconnect, posting a negative operating cash flow of Rs -5.80 Cr and a dismal cash conversion ratio of -1.44x against reported profit in March 2026 [E26, E27]. This cash burn deepens into a free cash flow deficit of Rs -16.09 Cr for the same period [E28], driven partly by soaring working capital requirements as debtor days balloon to an alarming 198 days and overall working capital days surge from 45.6 days to 114 days [E43, E44]. To fund these operational strains, the company has ramped up its borrowings to Rs 20.18 Cr in March 2026, up from Rs 13.92 Cr the prior year [E31], increasing its leverage load alongside an inconsistent operating margin trend across recent quarters and years [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the business offers a 0.00% dividend yield and explicitly flags a negative record of retaining all earnings instead of paying out dividends despite reported profits [E4, E42]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong multi-year sales and profit uptrends paired with a high historical ROE track record [E14, E17, E41].
